scope: Surviving five-bastion fort exterior, intrinsic courtyard wings/central dividing block, main entrance/bell structure and Kat balcony pediment. Keep original native courtyard voids. Detached town buildings, railway, moat/landscape reconstruction and interiors excluded.

quallaSearch.notes: Started with published Qualla originals. Andrew Massyn PD-selfpediment and exactcirca1880original with PD South-Africabasis/date selected. Unclear atlas authorship, stylized round-fort engraving, monochrome derivative and unrelated regional images excluded. No external imagery needed.

originalReview.notes: Both full native Qualla originals inspected:2816x2112Andrew Massyn2006PD-selfcourtyard-pediment photograph, and circa1880original sepia photograph with the castle stone curtain behind the railway. Modern image shows a yellow ochre curved Baroque pediment/white heraldic relief and flanking Neptune/Mercury figures; original category places it in the courtyard(Kat balcony), not the outer main gate. Period photo controls plain battered stone wall/low coping only; railway/people/signals are excluded. The old atlas transfer has no recorded author and is excluded. The1689Tachard round-fort engraving is stylized/unreliable for the surviving star geometry and is excluded. Regional theatre/consulate images are unrelated. Current exact native geometry controls full plan and courtyard layout.

references.caption: Standard gauge suburban train entering Cape Town station behind a 2-4-0T locomotive on dual gauge track (4 ft 8½ in broad gauge and 3 ft 6 in Cape gauge) on the old Strand street crossing, with the Castle of Good Hope in the background.
